source.note: This bank records reusable decisions, not the private source tree or a scored model result.

label_semantics.positive: Evidence supports subtraction, consolidation, or a fail-visible correction.
label_semantics.negative: A nearby construct has an independent root and must be preserved.

examples: non-finite values, joint limits, collision, illegal contact, and force backoff
release, clearance, target, and settle ordering, including rebound and hold semantics
terminal observation freeze, environment isolation, and batch error isolation
execution-quality signals that must not overwrite hard task failure
the current reachable task path and its distinct hard safety gates
atomic publish, replace, discard, and partial-output cleanup
media and state sidecars verified through real disk readback
current schema, source identity, resume comparison, ledger, and explicit counts
archive CRC, real member hashes, deterministic rebuild, and release manifests
corruption, missing fields, timeline drift, and malformed current data
physical state/action meaning and bounded parallel validation
accelerator versions, device capability, and required kernel selection
hand-eye, mirror, rigid-transform, and tool-mount calibration relations
real camera projection, field of view, resolution, and physical clearance
known mathematical examples, unit conversions, clamp behavior, and invalid time steps
concurrency limits, resource bounds, and cleanup lifecycle

observations.title: Large snapshots versus focused integration evidence
observations.positive: A snapshot copies hundreds of configuration or topology fields from the same implementation and fails on harmless reshaping.
observations.negative: An exact serialized artifact is itself an externally reviewed wire or persistence contract.
observations.independent_oracle: A small set of cross-layer closure facts, or exact external bytes when the bytes are the contract.

observations.title: Group by failure domain, not historical test name
observations.positive: Several inputs reach the same production branch and the same observable failure, so one table-driven node is sufficient.
observations.negative: Non-finite input, limits, collision, force, rebound, missing depth, and invisible masks have distinct acceptance semantics.
observations.independent_oracle: Input equivalence class to production branch to observable result mapping.

observations.title: Private helper versus independent algorithm root
observations.positive: A private helper test derives inputs and expected values from the same implementation constants or steps.
observations.negative: The helper implements a stable mathematical, encoding, or safety rule with known examples or independent invariants.
observations.independent_oracle: Known numerical result, external format, geometric invariant, or public behavior.

observations.title: One-off experiment artifact versus managed fixture
observations.positive: A default test reads an untracked run output or developer-local package and otherwise skips or fails.
observations.negative: The input is tracked, created by the test, or provisioned as an explicit managed resource.
observations.independent_oracle: A clean checkout can reproduce the input and the asserted behavior.

observations.title: Obsolete fixture versus surviving behavior
observations.positive: An old fixture carries only retired behavior with no current producer or consumer.
observations.negative: A current behavior still needs a lower public seam or integration root after the old carrier is removed.
observations.independent_oracle: Test to behavior to current owner mapping.

observations.title: Manufactured dry-run success versus assembly dry-run
observations.positive: A production command invents observations or forces phases to report a capability that no backend executes.
observations.negative: A dry-run only parses, assembles, or validates a request and makes no execution claim.
observations.independent_oracle: A real backend boundary for capability claims; parser or assembly contract for non-executing dry-runs.

observations.title: Tracked output writes versus read-only source assets
observations.positive: A test reaches a builder whose configured output overwrites tracked compiled assets.
observations.negative: The test reads tracked source data but redirects every generated output to a temporary directory.
observations.independent_oracle: Worktree state remains byte-for-byte unchanged around the test suite.

observations.title: Future possibility versus current production owner
observations.positive: Only synthetic tests can enable a future camera, platform, or task variant.
observations.negative: An active config, controlled deployment, or owned work package selects the variant.
observations.independent_oracle: Reachability from a non-test production input.

observations.title: Registry and CLI loop versus public command
observations.positive: A registry entry, CLI, diagnostic module, config, and tests only reference one another after an experiment ends.
observations.negative: A current operator workflow or external consumer invokes the documented public command.
observations.independent_oracle: A caller outside the registry/CLI/diagnostic cluster.

observations.title: Self-digest versus independent identity
observations.positive: One producer writes a payload, digest, receipt, and validation conclusion from the same information.
observations.negative: A digest crosses publication, transport, resume, persisted readback, or a third-party consumer boundary.
observations.independent_oracle: Independently supplied digest, content identity, or corruption failure domain.

observations.title: Test-only compatibility alias versus supported stored data
observations.positive: An alias, legacy field, or diagnostic rule has no old producer, data inventory, external consumer, or retirement condition.
observations.negative: A current external consumer or stored-data population still requires the compatibility path under an explicit policy.
observations.independent_oracle: Named producer, consumer, data population, and sunset condition.

observations.title: Silent fallback versus explicit recovery contract
observations.positive: Malformed current data is reinterpreted through defaults, filenames, broad retries, or an old path.
observations.negative: An explicit version, missing-field rule, external error translation, or cleanup contract defines recovery.
observations.independent_oracle: Current producer schema or documented legacy protocol.

observations.title: Fake-only dependency skip versus real optional boundary
observations.positive: A fake-backed test skips when an SDK or simulator that it never calls is absent.
observations.negative: The test imports the SDK, compiles the real model, writes through the codec, or calls the optional backend.
observations.independent_oracle: The dependency is present on the executed call path.

observations.title: Coverage-created branch versus active safety path
observations.positive: Tests mutate thresholds or call post-gate helpers to cover a branch no active config can reach.
observations.negative: The current task reaches the branch, or the adjacent guard enforces a distinct hard safety failure.
observations.independent_oracle: Active configuration and separate safety acceptance semantics.

observations.title: Green endpoints versus a closed production path
observations.positive: A retired cross-layer fixture has no current identity or consumer and can be removed as a cluster.
observations.negative: Producer, loader, and state machine pass separately, but no test proves that the current identity crosses their edges.
observations.independent_oracle: One hermetic current producer-to-reader-to-consumer integration root.

observations.title: Conditional integrity versus explicit optional enrichment
observations.positive: A declared package-level artifact is verified only when its file happens to exist, allowing lower-level sidecars to take over authority.
observations.negative: The protocol explicitly marks an enrichment artifact optional and defines behavior when it is absent.
observations.independent_oracle: Package declaration and digest contract, not filesystem presence.

observations.title: Main-loader schema bump versus explicit migration reader
observations.positive: The writer and canonical loader reject old data while a CLI, visualizer, or tool still hand-parses and accepts it.
observations.negative: A separately named migration reader intentionally accepts a documented old version.
observations.independent_oracle: Every current public deserialize boundary enforces the shared version; migration boundaries are explicit.

observations.title: Critical-field default versus optional presentation default
observations.positive: A required identity, source path, count, or handedness field still has a historical dataclass or parser default.
observations.negative: A presentation or enrichment field is explicitly optional and has defined default behavior.
observations.independent_oracle: Type, parser, and validator agree on requiredness.

observations.title: Stale current docs versus labeled history
observations.positive: Authoritative PLAN, STATUS, architecture, or workflow text still promises a removed fallback or marks a completed fix as pending.
observations.negative: A history, migration note, or future proposal is clearly labeled and does not describe the current path.
observations.independent_oracle: Current callers and active configuration agree with current-facing documentation.
